The original 1996 FERC applications proposed a materially different, since-superseded mainline design (241.9 mi/20-in from North Troy VT to Haverhill MA per the May 1996 NOI, later amended to 224.1 mi/20-in from Pittsburg NH to Haverhill MA plus 48.4 mi of laterals per the Dec 1996 amended notice) -- neither of those figures matches 295 either, but both predate decades of subsequent capacity/compression projects (C2C, PXP I-III, WXP I-III) that did not add material new mainline pipe (LengthKnown=0 on the XPress rows), so the original design mileage is not a live current-length source. The original 1996 design capacity was 178,000 Mcf/d (178 MMcf/d) peak day, per the May 1996 NOI -- about 18% below 210, too far off for a rounding match, and in any case describing the superseded North-Troy-VT-to-Haverhill-MA design, not the built Pittsburg-NH-to-Westbrook-ME system. This pattern makes it highly likely the true current wholly-owned-system capacity is well above 210 MMcf/d and above the 1996 178 MMcf/d design figure, but no single citable source states one current aggregate wholly-owned-system capacity number as of a specific recent date (a detailed capacity-growth table exists in an internal industry-association PDF, but no public URL for it could be found or reconstructed this session, so it cannot be cited per the never-fabricate-a-URL rule). Recommend flagging Capacity as likely stale rather than proposing an unsourced replacement number.
